portfolioProgress.title: Portfolio progress
portfolioProgress.body: What this shows: how far along each project is, as one number per project. How it is calculated: it takes every task in the project that is not cancelled, treats each task's completion percentage equally, and averages them. A task at 40 percent contributes 40. What is excluded: archived projects are not counted at all.
portfolioProgress.formula: average of task progress percent, excluding cancelled tasks

projectProgress.title: Project progress
projectProgress.body: What this shows: how far along this project is right now. How it is calculated: it averages the completion percentage of every task in the project that is not cancelled, weighting each task equally. A completed or verified task counts as 100. What is excluded: cancelled tasks.
projectProgress.formula: average of task progress percent, excluding cancelled tasks

progressOverTime.title: Progress over time
progressOverTime.body: What this shows: whether the project is ahead of or behind its plan. How it is calculated: the actual line is the project progress recorded at the end of each day from submitted daily reports. The planned line is a straight line from the project start date to the planned end date. What is excluded: days with no report are not gaps, they carry the previous day's figure forward.
progressOverTime.formula: planned = (days since start / total planned days) x 100

labourHeadcount.title: Labour headcount trend
labourHeadcount.body: What this shows: how many people were on this site on each of the last thirty days. How it is calculated: it counts every worker marked present or half day on that date at this project. A half day counts as one person, not half, because this chart is about how many people were on site. What is excluded: absent workers, and the money view, which is on the labour cost chart.
labourHeadcount.formula: count of workers with day value above 0

labourCost.title: Labour cost by category
labourCost.body: What this shows: what the labour on this site cost each week, split by worker category. How it is calculated: for each worker it adds up the daily rate multiplied by the day value from attendance, plus overtime, then groups the totals by category and by week. What is excluded: advances are not subtracted here, because this chart shows cost incurred, not cash still to hand over.
labourCost.formula: (daily rate x day value) + (overtime hours x daily rate / 8)

wagesPayable.title: Wages payable
wagesPayable.body: What this shows: the amount owed to this worker for the selected period, before any statutory deductions. How it is calculated: for each day, the worker's daily rate is multiplied by the day value from attendance, where present counts as 1 and half day counts as 0.5. Overtime hours are paid at the rate divided by 8, per hour. Any advances recorded in the period are then subtracted. What is excluded: provident fund, employee state insurance, and tax. SiteLedger does not calculate statutory payroll.
wagesPayable.formula: (daily rate x day value) + (overtime hours x daily rate / 8) - advances

topMaterials.title: Top materials consumed
topMaterials.body: What this shows: which materials this site used most in the period you picked. How it is calculated: it adds up the quantity issued from store to site for each material across the range. What is excluded: material that has been received but is still sitting in store is not counted, because it has not been consumed yet.
topMaterials.formula: sum of issue movements per item

stockOnHand.title: Stock on hand
stockOnHand.body: What this shows: how much of each material is physically at this site right now. How it is calculated: it is total received minus total issued for that item at that site, read from the movement ledger every time. The marker on the bar is the low stock threshold you set on the item. What is excluded: nothing. Stock is never stored as a number, so a correction to any receipt or issue updates it immediately.
stockOnHand.formula: received + transfers in - issued - transfers out

spendByCategory.title: Spend by category
spendByCategory.body: What this shows: where the money on this project went, month by month. How it is calculated: it adds approved expenses, the value of goods actually received on purchase orders, wages payable, and equipment rental and repair costs, then groups them by category. What is excluded: expenses that are still waiting for approval are not included, and ordered goods that have not arrived are not included.
spendByCategory.formula: approved expenses + received goods value + wages payable + equipment costs

issueAgeing.title: Issue ageing
issueAgeing.body: What this shows: how long the open issues on this project have been waiting. How it is calculated: it groups open issues by how many days since they were raised, into 0 to 2, 3 to 7, 8 to 14, and over 14. What is excluded: resolved and closed issues are not counted, because this chart is about backlog.

taskStatus.title: Task status
taskStatus.body: What this shows: how the work on this project is distributed across the task lifecycle. How it is calculated: it counts the tasks in each status. What is excluded: overdue is not a status, it is any task past its due date that is not completed or verified, so a task can be both in progress and overdue.

equipmentUtilisation.title: Equipment utilisation
equipmentUtilisation.body: What this shows: how hard each machine and reusable set worked in the period. How it is calculated: days in use is the number of days the asset was allocated to a site, read from the movement log. Days idle is the number of days it sat in the yard, or at a site with no allocation. What is excluded: days under repair are shown separately and counted in neither.
equipmentUtilisation.formula: days between movements, attributed to the state after each movement

purchaseOrderStatus.title: Purchase order status
purchaseOrderStatus.body: What this shows: where every purchase order stands. How it is calculated: it counts purchase orders by status. Pending quantity is ordered quantity minus received quantity across all goods receipts raised against that order. What is excluded: cancelled orders are shown but never counted as pending.
purchaseOrderStatus.formula: ordered quantity - sum of received quantity

dprCompliance.title: Daily report compliance
dprCompliance.body: What this shows: whether each site is actually submitting its daily report. How it is calculated: it compares the number of reports submitted against the number expected, which is one per active site per working day, over the last fourteen days. What is excluded: Sundays and any date before the project start date are not counted as expected.

spendToDate.title: Spend to date
spendToDate.body: What this shows: the total money committed on this project so far. How it is calculated: approved expenses, plus the value of goods actually received against purchase orders, plus wages payable from attendance, plus equipment rental and repair costs. What is excluded: expenses awaiting approval, and goods ordered but not yet delivered.
spendToDate.formula: approved expenses + received goods + wages payable + equipment costs

budgetUsed.title: Budget used
budgetUsed.body: What this shows: how much of the budget you set on this project has been committed. How it is calculated: spend to date divided by the project budget. What is excluded: if no budget was set on the project, this figure is not shown at all rather than guessed.
budgetUsed.formula: spend to date / project budget x 100

idleDays.title: Idle days
idleDays.body: What this shows: how long this asset has been sitting without a site to work on. How it is calculated: it counts the days since the movement that left the asset with no site allocation, read from the movement log. What is excluded: time under repair does not count as idle, and an asset currently checked out to a site shows zero.
idleDays.formula: days since the last movement that left the asset unallocated

openCritical.title: Open critical issues
openCritical.body: What this shows: how many serious problems are unresolved across your projects right now. How it is calculated: it counts issues at high or critical priority whose status is not resolved and not closed. What is excluded: low and medium priority issues.
openCritical.formula: count of open issues at high or critical priority

verified.title: Verified
verified.body: What this shows: that someone with authority checked the work was actually done, not just marked done. How it is set: only a project manager, an owner, or a site engineer can move a task to verified. A supervisor cannot, in the interface or through the database. What is excluded: completing a task is not the same as verifying it.

halfDay.title: Half day
halfDay.body: What this shows: that the worker was on site for part of the day. How it is used: a half day counts as 0.5 when wages are calculated, and as one person when headcount is counted. What is excluded: it does not change the overtime rate.

reusableSet.title: Reusable set
reusableSet.body: What this shows: shuttering, formwork or scaffolding tracked as one object with a quantity, rather than as individual panels or clamps. How it is used: the whole set moves between sites as a unit and accumulates idle days as a unit. What is excluded: individual components are not tracked, because counting clamps is what makes a register nobody keeps up to date.

neededBy.title: Needed by
neededBy.body: What this shows: the date the site actually needs the material in hand, not the date it was requested. How it is used: it drives the ordering priority on the procurement desk and flags requests that will arrive late. What is excluded: it is not a promise date from the vendor, that is the expected delivery on the purchase order.
